"This is not cyber attack, and this is not a coordinated effort by a nation state," he told CNBC's "Closing Bell" on Tuesday. "We've looked very closely." It's been a tough few days for the technology world after series of widespread disruptions brought different parts of life to a halt. On Tuesday, an outage halted internal communications at the National Security Agency and iPhone maker Apple confirmed that different products were either down or having issues . The NSA pointed to "scheduled routine maintenance," while Apple cited "an internal update" as the reason behind each issue. It marked four major system problems in four consecutive business days. watch now VIDEO 2:13 02:13 Apple: Many of our systems back up and running after an internal update caused some outages Power Lunch Microsoft 's Outlook issues wreaked havoc on businesses on Thursday, and the Federal Aviation Administration grounded flights on Friday. On Monday, issues at JPMorgan Chase affected customer transactions and an outage at United Airlines briefly delayed departing flights. "When Microsoft goes down, the whole world comes to a standstill," said Raj Rajamani, CEO of JetStream Security. "That's a stark reminder of how deeply embedded these services and technologies are in our day-to-day life." The disruptions have rattled consumers and led to a steady stream of memes on social media, as people look for a silver lining — or sinister plot — in the string of technology problems. Experts say the real culprit behind this strange series of coincidences is much more benign. "We're in the weird teenage phase of technology not quite maturing enough to know how to do this without disrupting services and so forth," said Tom Hegel, research head at SentinelOne. The FAA, which is still looking into the root cause of the system failure, pointed in part to a router upgrade in southern Arkansas overseen by government contractor L3Harris Technologies that overwhelmed the agency's telecommunications network. JPMorgan said longer-than-usual service times on Monday stemmed from a software bug in on-premise hardware systems. The embattled chipmaker is slated to release its results after the market close. Software stocks also slipped in the session's sell-off, with Salesforce, Palo Alto Networks and Oracle dropping. Follow along as CNBC highlights the biggest stock market moves of the day. 1 Hour Ago Solar ETF tumbles to lowest level since August 2025 The Invesco Solar ETF (TAN) dropped roughly 5% in afternoon trading, sliding to its lowest level since August 2025. The Invesco Solar ETF (TAN) on Tuesday The fall also places the ETF on pace for its worst session since June 5, 2026. Enphase Energy, First Solar and SolarEdge dragged the ETF lower, with the three stocks touching at least 52-week lows. The declines occur as the Dec. 4 effective date for President Trump's Section 232 tariffs on solar products approaches. -- Darla Mercado, Gina Francolla 4 Hours Ago Nvidia ticks lower ahead of results Gene Medi | Nurphoto | Getty Images Nvidia shares flipped negative on the day and were last down more than 1% as its quarterly report loomed. The company's third-quarter report , due after Tuesday's market close, comes less than a week after co-founder Jensen Huang resigned as CEO. Nvidia on Tuesday Huang, in his first public statement since leaving the helm, also indicated in a written statement obtained by CNBC's David Faber that he would be willing to come back as CEO. "If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO," Huang said in the statement. -- Darla Mercado, Kif Leswing 4 Hours Ago Software stocks tumble as traders shun tech Software companies were caught up in Tuesday's sell off, with the iShares Expanded Tech-Software Sector ETF (IGV) down more than 3% on the day. The iShares Expanded Tech-Software Sector ETF (IGV) in Tuesday's trading Salesforce plummeted nearly 10%, while cybersecurity play Palo Alto Networks and cloud platform service giant Oracle both lost 4%. Microsoft and Palantir slid 3%. — Darla Mercado 4 Hours Ago SpaceX rises on Bloomberg report that some of its debt could soon go on sale Elon Musk's SpaceX rose Tuesday afternoon following a Bloomberg report that a tranche of the company's $40 billion in debt financing could be sold to investors as early as this week. Bloomberg, which cited people with knowledge of the matter, said that around $4 billion of these bonds could go on the market in the approaching days. SpaceX aims to use this debt sale to cover the cost of artificial intelligence chips, Bloomberg reported. SpaceX was last up almost 3% on the day. SpaceX on Tuesday — Darla Mercado 6 Hours Ago TD Cowen names Coca-Cola top pick for 2027 A Coca-Cola sign is seen in Atlanta on April 15, 2025. Elijah Nouvelage | Afp | Getty Images Shares of Coca-Cola are down a fraction after TD Cowen named the soft drink maker its best idea for 2027, citing pricing power, global reach and Coke's franchise bottling system. TD Cowen reiterated Coke's buy rating and raised its 12-month price target to $112 from $104, implying roughly 13% upside from Monday's close. Coca-Cola is ahead 42% so far in 2026 "The company's international footprint and advantaged franchise bottling system position KO for on-algorithm 5% organic sales growth, well above [consumer packaged goods] peers," said the bank's analyst Robert Moskow. "Despite the stock's rise this year, we think it will move higher as KO proves they can overcome rising inflation and tough comparisons," the analyst wrote Tuesday. — Deena Zaidi 6 Hours Ago Bernstein downgrades PepsiCo, sees 13% downside Illuminated logo for Pepsi on a soda fountain in Walnut Creek, California, March 4, 2026. Smith Collection | Gado | Archive Photos | Getty Images Share of PepsiCo were down nearly 2% after Bernstein downgraded the Gatorade and Frito-Lay snack maker to underperform from market-perform. The brokerage and researcher also cut its price target to $128, implying roughly 13% downside from Monday's close, from an earlier $131. Bernstein also cut its 2027 adjusted earnings estimate to $8.27 per share from $8.49.
